thesis:
One sentence holds the whole file together: at a ~5% risk-free rate with $365tn of global debt, the marginal dollar stops buying narrative and starts buying chokepoints. Every recurring observation across six weeks points the same direction — electrons, molecules, memory bits, fab capacity, transmission, fuel cycle, payment/exchange rails, and now the agent identity-and-containment layer. These are the places where a fundamental human need (energy, security, productivity, time) meets a physically or legally constrained supply. The AI story has quietly stopped being a semiconductor story and become a power-industrial and governance story: Meta funding seven gas plants, Amazon's $8bn Generac order, Mitsui contracting LNG explicitly for data centers, ERCOT's 2030s load curve, Italy and Poland reversing nuclear policy, Korea's reported $200bn into US nuclear/LNG/gas. Generation and grid regain pricing power lost for forty years. The financing of the buildout is getting circular (vendor equity, insurer-wrapped GPU loans, vendor-linked cloud commitments), which tells you the eventual drawdown is a capital-structure event, not a demand event — the electrons will still be needed when the equity of the second-tier neoclouds is wiped out. That asymmetry is the single most important portfolio construction insight in the dataset: own the constraint, rent the narrative.

On the human side, the dominant behavioural rotation is from convenience to security, and from intelligence to time. Consumers and enterprises are buying guaranteed electrons, audit trails, fraud protection, and reclaimed hours. The fastest-rising consumer queries are not 'better chatbot' but 'ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service', 'ai agent builder' — people are purchasing delegation of the lowest-status use of their time, and then they will immediately demand proof of containment over what acts in their name. That is why cybersecurity converts from a defensive cost centre into a metered utility on every agent action: the most defensible annuity in the AI stack, more durable than model licences or GPU rental. Simultaneously, the housing need goes unmet but is *financed away from* rather than resolved: 7%+ mortgages freeze turnover, capital rotates out of dwellings into data centers (Kashkari's framing), and the behavioural adaptation is renovation-over-relocation, longer tenancy, smaller and manufactured formats, multigenerational households. The durable trade is maintenance, MRO and rental economics — not homebuilding volume.

Third, aging and the 2029 inflection to shrinking Western populations make productivity-per-worker the only growth lever and public finance the permanent source of term premium. That single fact underwrites automation, agents, healthspan and hard assets simultaneously, and it caps the multiple on anything long-duration and non-cash-generative. Health demand is visibly shifting from managed disease to restored function and continuous measurement — the 107% surge in robotic-surgery intent spanning hysterectomy, hernia, prostate, knee is an aging cohort shopping for the machine that will operate on it, and the dataset flags it as unpriced. Note the one genuine contradiction in the record: the 2026-09-25 brief argues metabolic management is going pharmacological and *away* from device-and-discipline models, raising the bar for CGM franchises, while 2026-10-05 reasserts continuous monitoring. I resolve this toward procedures/devices-for-function (robotic surgery, cardiac, orthopedic) plus GLP-1 pharmacology, and treat standalone CGM-as-wellness as the weaker leg.

Finally, market structure is being unbundled across time (24/7, weekend, tokenized equities at 11% of DEX volume), access (SEC retail private-asset proposals, investor exam) and venue (TXSE $80bn of listings, Schwab listing there, NSE India, Manila IPOs). The value accrues to rails, venues and brokers, not to asset gatherers — and it quietly pushes illiquidity onto households late in a cycle, which is a tail risk to own via the intermediary rather than the asset. For capital: overweight the power-compute complex, memory/optics, agent-governance security, exchange/broker rails and the renovation economy; underweight anything whose moat was cheap capital, anything priced on seats, and model-layer pure plays whose terminal economics are contestable by edge inference.

theme_ranking.why: The most repeated, most corroborated shift in the entire record: eight separate briefs independently conclude electricity is the binding constraint on AI. Generation gets pricing power it has not had in decades, demand is contracted multi-year by the strongest balance sheets in the world, and the flow data (Utilities at -87/-94) says the market has not marked it. Highest conviction, with the added asymmetry that the electrons are needed even if AI equity financing breaks.

Converts from defensive cost centre to metered utility on every agent action. Non-discretionary, recurring, and newly expanded by agent identity/containment — a budget line that did not exist three years ago. Tops all flow rankings and is reinforced by Interpol/AI-scam evidence, enterprise model restrictions and the absence of statutory law (private standard wins first). Pricing at 65 is the only thing holding conviction below 0.85.

Trend 61 with narrative 84 and attention 77 means the story is fully told; the durable claim is on the physical layer (memory, optics, networking, fab capacity) rather than on compute landlords. Circular vendor financing is the real risk, and it argues for owning the constraint-holders inside the theme and avoiding the levered neocloud middle.

The direct derivative of power-demand with a longer, more regulated and less reflexive revenue stream: transmission EPC, switchgear, turbines, behind-the-meter flexibility. Quanta raising outlook, Emerald AI grid-headroom venture, grid resilience now priced as a security asset after military targeting. Trend only 40 vs narrative 71 — the gap is the opportunity.

Memory and fab capacity are the tightest links and the least exposed to a frontier-model training pause, since inference and edge deployment consume HBM/DRAM regardless of training cadence. Sovereignty capex (Micron Sanand, reshoring) adds a policy-funded floor. Offset: pricing 68 is the highest in the set, so much is already in.

Agents are being bought as time, not intelligence — the clearest consumer-level behavioural signal in the dataset. But narrative 84 vs trend 66 and the collapse of seat-based pricing mean value accrues unevenly: to incumbents with distribution and to the governance layer, not to standalone model vendors. Conviction in the shift is higher than conviction in most of the equities.

Attention 82 in-brief with the fastest-rising consumer query set, Apple's cost-per-token economics, Meta shipping a consumer device, fiber capex following inference to the edge. The structural bet is that inference cost — not peak FLOPs — becomes the purchase criterion, which reallocates margin from compute landlords to silicon and devices.

Gas is the marginal AI fuel for the next three years and LNG is now contracted explicitly for data centers. Energy security has become sovereign capex rather than commodity cyclicality — Korean $200bn, Mitsui, pipeline capacity races, a proposed diesel export ban. Discounted slightly because commodity price is the swing factor and pricing at 56 is not cheap.

Unbundling across time, venue and access is happening simultaneously and is already regulator-sanctioned. Rails, venues and brokers capture value whether the underlying assets perform or not — a genuine toll road. Risk: pushing illiquid private assets to retail late in a cycle creates a reputational/regulatory reversal scenario.

The demographic fuse (shrinking Western populations from ~2029) plus skilled-trade scarcity makes labour substitution the only growth lever. Procurement has started (5,000-unit Optimus order, Japan's national physical-AI infrastructure) but the market now demands unit economics, and construction robotics explicitly will not fix housing this cycle. High certainty on direction, low certainty on timing and on who captures the margin.

Policy reversals are real and multi-decade — Italy after 40 years, Poland's mega-project, US AI-driven restart support, record Chinese output, uranium at record highs. But trend is only 35 against narrative 73, equities have slid while the commodity rose, and the cash flows arrive in the 2030s. Own the fuel cycle and the existing merchant fleet, not the developer promise.

Supply-chain sovereignty, not tariffs, is the long war; China's rare-earth leverage and EU trade weapons make this a multi-decade policy-funded spend. The honest caveat is that industrial flows are negative today — this is a structurally right theme that pays slowly and lumpily.

The 107% robotic-surgery query surge with granular procedural intent is the single cleanest unpriced demand signal in the dataset, corroborated by Medtronic's raise. An aging cohort shopping for restored function is a 10-year tailwind. Trend 37 and pricing 46 say the market is treating it as a mature medtech cycle, not a demographic one.

Deficits, $365tn of debt, suspect inflation measurement and an administration framing inflation as debt rebalancing all support it. But the record is honest that the 'store of value' need is currently being met by 5% yield, not metal — gold hit a seven-week low while Treasuries absorbed the flow. Right over a decade, poorly timed while real rates rise.

Data-centre buildout plus grid modernisation collide with constrained supply; the physics is unarguable. Discounted because pricing at 64 is already elevated and the thesis depends on a macro scare passing rather than on anything idiosyncratic.

Trend 69 with attention 71 and pricing 60 — well understood and well owned. Azure at 43% proves the demand, but the market has now explicitly separated monetisation from spending, and the cloud layer sits between two parties with more pricing power: the silicon/memory suppliers below and the agent/distribution layer above.

The only theme flagged attention_not_priced=true, at attention 71 against pricing 45. The agent transaction layer is a genuine re-plumbing of ad economics and TikTok Shop plus live sports rights are the largest unmonetized attention pool noted. Conviction is capped because the winner is genuinely undetermined — Meta, Google and Amazon are fighting over who holds intent.

Military targeting of energy and compute infrastructure converts resilience from cyclical capex to a policy-mandated line, and stockpiling (UK tungsten) is already happening. But trend 41 against narrative 73 is the classic signature of a theme where the story runs far ahead of order books and budget appropriation.

Rails are good businesses in a fragmenting world (Kazakhstan-China QR, Tencent for inbound tourists, GCash/Mynt IPOs, next billion financial relationships forming outside US platforms). Offset by the emerging stablecoin threat to pure card-network toll economics — a decade risk, not a quarter risk, but it caps terminal multiples.

Consumer bifurcation is well evidenced and recurring — Walmart raising guidance, dollar-store attention, Nike's worst year, mid-tier dining slowdown. It is a real and durable behavioural shift but a low-margin, well-understood one with limited multiple expansion available.

Tokenized equities at 11% of DEX volume with SEC approval and stablecoin attention up 53-64% are genuine structural plumbing changes, not speculation. I rank it below market-structure because the rail owners and brokers capture the volume more reliably than the tokens themselves.

$250k/yr longevity care and Grail attention +180% establish a premium tier that historically trickles down into diagnostics and screening. Early, narrow, and with unproven reimbursement — a real need with an immature business model.

Supported by delivery aggregation replacing personal trips as mobility is repriced, and by agentic commerce. But the diesel/distillate squeeze taxes delivery economics directly, which is a margin headwind the attention-driven version of this theme ignores.

Einride scaling autonomous freight, Nvidia under major robotaxi programmes, and 'why buying trucks stops making sense' fleet economics are all real. Trend 57 with attention 28 says it is underfollowed, but the capital intensity and regulatory timeline keep returns a decade out.

Starship reaching orbit genuinely compresses the mass-to-orbit cost curve and orbital compute (Google, SpaceX/Nvidia) is a live siting answer to the power problem. But attention 66 against trend 54 means the narrative is already ahead of revenue, and in-space compute is a 2030s cash flow.

Demand is unquestionable and Lilly is taking share, but the dataset describes a 'GLP-1 war' with Novo rebranding and strategy rethinks — competitive intensity is destroying the pricing power that made this theme investable. Own the need, be very selective on the equity.

The shortage is real and will not resolve — but the record is explicit that it is financed away from rather than fixed, with capital rotating into data centers. Trend 29 and narrative 16 are consistent with that. The durable expression is renovation, MRO and rental economics, not homebuilder volume; as a theme ID it ranks low even though the underlying need is permanent.

The reallocation of leisure into the home is a genuine durable shift (more US cards pay for streaming than cinema and concerts combined) but it is a mature, competitive, content-cost-inflating industry. The behaviour is right; the economics do not reward the observer.

Genuinely bifurcated: Carnival's record $7.6B deposits versus Ryanair cutting winter capacity and Norwegian near 52-week lows. Demand exists but operators cannot sell it profitably at $100+ crude, and the segment carries the cheap-capital moat problem the whole record warns about. Lowest conviction in the set.

beneficiary_profiles: Constraint owners: merchant and regulated generators with data-center load, transmission capacity holders, fuel-cycle and uranium owners — entities that can say no to a hyperscaler.

Picks-and-shovels for the power-compute merge: gas turbine and switchgear OEMs, behind-the-meter generation, electrical EPC and mechanical contractors, cooling. The labour scarcity (electricians, HVAC, pipefitters) is itself the moat.

Metered-utility security: vendors whose revenue scales per agent, per identity or per action rather than per seat — the only AI line item that grows with deployment volume and is legally non-discretionary.

Toll roads on fragmentation: exchanges, brokers, custody and settlement rails that earn on volume and venue count regardless of asset direction — they monetize uncertainty and 24/7 behaviour rather than returns.
Tight-link component suppliers: HBM/DRAM, optics, fiber, networking silicon — exposed to inference volume rather than training cadence, hence less sensitive to a frontier-model pause.
Repair-and-stay-put beneficiaries: home improvement retail, MRO distributors, rental operators and maintenance supply chains that capture the housing budget when transactions freeze.
Restored-function healthcare: robotic surgery platforms and cardiac/ortho device annuities selling to an aging cohort that actively shops procedures.
Sovereign-capex recipients: domestic fabs, materials processing, defence stockpiles and grid hardening funded by policy allocation rather than by return-on-capital math.
Distribution incumbents in agentic software: companies that can bundle agents into existing seats and prove auditability, versus standalone model vendors with no channel.

Structural avoids: businesses whose moat was cheap capital — marginal homebuilders, levered consumer lenders, REIT roll-ups, second-tier neoclouds, pre-revenue narrative IPOs, and anything still priced per seat.

Starship reaching orbit compresses the mass-to-orbit cost curve for everyone, and orbital compute plus defence constellations are genuine new demand. Space narrative 67 vs trend 54 means it is a story stock, but the launch-cadence supply chain is the under-modelled part.

Advertising-attention is the only theme flagged attention_not_priced=true (attention 71, pricing 45). Meta is the most aggressive bidder for the agent transaction layer — Muse, consumer AI device, $1,299 glasses, the Amazon agent-access standoff — and is being punished for capex at exactly the moment it is buying the intent layer and its own generation.
Duplicate-safe note: optical and fiber content per AI edge deployment is rising faster than consensus models assume as inference distributes.

anti_theses: 'Own the model layer.' The record repeatedly shows value migrating away from frontier models: enterprises restricting Anthropic over data fears, Apple's cost-per-token economics, inference moving to devices, seat pricing collapsing. Model licences are the least defensible annuity in the stack; identity, containment, memory bits and electrons are the defensible ones.

'Centralized GPU rental is the terminal business model.' Edge inference, efficiency-per-token purchase criteria, insurer-wrapped GPU loans extending credit to smaller clouds, and vendor-linked cloud commitments all say compute landlords face contestable terminal value and embedded credit risk. Near-term order books are booming; that is not the same thing.

'China AI semiconductor revenue returns.' Huawei's Ascend 960 on a Q1 2027 timetable plus explicit sovereignty policy means Western accelerator TAM in China should be modelled toward zero. Treating it as recovery optionality is a recurring consensus error in the record.

'Rates revert to 3% and housing unfreezes.' $365tn of global debt, shrinking Western populations from 2029, sovereign competition for capital at every auction and suspect inflation measurement all argue term premium stays elevated. Underwriting equities against a reversion is the most widely held unsupported assumption here.

'The housing shortage is a homebuilder trade.' The shortage is real but is being financed away from, not resolved — capital rotating into data centers, builders cutting price rather than volume, construction robotics explicitly years away. The need converts into rental, remodel and multigenerational economics, not into starts.

'Gold is working as the inflation hedge right now.' The record is blunt: gold hit a seven-week low while 19-year-high Treasury yields absorbed the capital. The store-of-value need is currently being met by yield. Gold is a decade thesis being sold as a present-tense trade.
'GLP-1 is a secular winner for all participants.' A share war with Novo rebranding and rethinking strategy is the signature of pricing power eroding. The need compounds; the margin pool may not.

'AI capex will break on a demand failure.' Every brief says the opposite — demand is real and self-funding at the hyperscaler level. The failure mode is the circular financing structure, which means the drawdown hits the levered middle, not the constraint owners. Shorting the constraint as an AI hedge is the wrong trade.

'Continuous glucose monitoring becomes default healthspan infrastructure.' Flagged early in the record, then contradicted on 2026-09-25: metabolic management is going pharmacological, which raises the bar for CGM to prove incremental value. The device-and-discipline model is the weaker leg of the health thesis.

'Cybersecurity is a mature, GDP-growth category.' Agent identity, delegated authority and per-action containment create a budget line that did not exist three years ago and scales with deployment volume rather than headcount. The category's TAM math is being underwritten on the old unit.
what_would_change: Electricity prices or interconnect queues easing materially — if data centers start getting power on demand at reasonable cost, the entire power-as-constraint thesis loses its scarcity premium and the capital rotates back to compute.

A hyperscaler cutting capex guidance for demand reasons rather than discipline reasons. That would convert the thesis from 'financing event' to 'demand event' and invalidate the claim that constraint owners are protected by contracted load.

Statutory federal AI safety law superseding Nvidia's private reference architecture. Public mandate would commoditize the governance layer and transfer the toll from vendors to compliance checkboxes — it would make agent governance a cost, not an annuity.

The 10-year sustainably below ~3.5%. That single change un-freezes housing turnover, rehabilitates the cheap-capital business models the thesis writes off, kills the renovation-over-relocation substitution, and makes long-duration narrative assets investable again.

Local political resistance to data centers (water usage, 'ai data center near me', electricity bills entering household tariffs) producing siting moratoria in two or more major load regions. That caps the buildout at the permitting layer rather than the power layer and changes who wins.

Edge inference failing on cost or capability — if device-based tokens prove materially more expensive or worse than cloud inference, the edge-AI margin reallocation reverses and compute landlords reclaim terminal value.

A credit event at a second-tier neocloud or an insurer-wrapped GPU loan book. That would validate the circular-financing warning, and I would expect indiscriminate selling that temporarily hits constraint owners — a buying signal, not a thesis break, unless contracted load is cancelled.

Robotic-surgery and device demand showing up in reimbursement cuts rather than volume growth. The 107% query surge is intent; if payers ration the procedure, the healthspan thesis stalls at the demand stage.
Humanoid or construction robotics posting credible unit economics (not orders) — that would pull the robotics-automation and housing-cost theses forward by years and justify a much higher ranking.

A regulatory reversal on retail private-market access or tokenized equities after a retail illiquidity blow-up. The market-structure toll road thesis depends on the unbundling continuing; a scandal-driven rollback would hit venues and brokers hardest.

Stablecoin volume crossing into actual merchant settlement share rather than search interest. That moves the card-network disruption from a 3-7 year speculation to a live revenue threat and would force a downgrade of digital-payments incumbents.
Inflation re-accelerating with real rates falling — that flips gold from the yield-loser it currently is to the primary hedge, and would substantially raise conviction in gold-hard-assets.
